newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GERMAN GREENS TOP CZECH POLITICIANS IN SOCCER FRIENDLY.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN GREENS TOP CZECH POLITICIANS IN SOCCER FRIENDLY.

text.p: Visiting German politicians trounced their Czech counterparts on Sunday in a friendly soccer match that offered a break from the more serious goal of negotiating a joint reconciliation agreement between the two countries.

Bonn and Prague have for months been trying to hammer out a text intended to set aside lingering resentment over both the Nazi invasion of Czechoslovakia and the expulsion of millions of ethnic Germans from the country after World War Two.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl says the declaration will be ready this year. Czech Deputy Foreign Minister and team captain Alexandr Vondra added Sunday that he saw no reason why the Czech-German document could not be signed at the executive level by the end of the year.

Representatives of Germany's opposition Greens party dominated the Czech political "all-stars" throughout the match, but only broke it open late in the first half with two quick strikes before coasting to a 3:0 victory.

"Perhaps we could hold (a rematch) on the occasion of the speech of the the Czech president, who will address the German parliament on the signing of the declaration," said Greens team captain and parliamentary faction head Joschka Fischer. "In that event, we could request a little pre-game."

Bundestag deputy Jafari-Gorzini Mehdi sparked the Germans with two goals, the first on a penalty kick and the second a rocket from the left side of the goal late in the game, while Fischer scored on a header late in the first half.

"I've come to understand that Germany, as a democratic state for decades, is in a slightly different situation and that politicians there have far more time for football," quipped Czech parliamentary deputy Michal Lobkowicz after the match.

As for his team's lacklustre performance on the soccer pitch, Czech captain Vondra made no excuses: "It didn't quite come off, but as they say: 'Tough on the practice field, easy on the battlefield'." REUTER
